summary: A 100-foot Georgia Forestry Commission tower at Bostwick was announced in 1957 to be moved to Apalachee, Morgan County; no source confirms the move.

events.note: Move from Bostwick to Apalachee announced in January 1957 as planned; the sources do not confirm completion

evidence.supports: Move from Bostwick to Apalachee announced, January 1957
evidence.quote: The Georgia Forestry Commission Morgan fire tower now located at Bostwick will be moved to Apalachee as soon as possible, Morgan-Walton Ranger Harold Jones announced this week.

evidence.supports: Move from Bostwick to Apalachee announced, January 1957
evidence.quote: The Georgia Forestry Commission Morgan fire tower now located at Bostwick will be moved to Apalachee as soon as possible, Morgan-Walton Ranger Harold Jones announced this week.

evidence.supports: 100-foot tower; purpose was better coverage of Morgan and Walton forests
evidence.quote: The 100-foot-tall tower is being moved to provide better coverage of Morgan and Walton County forests, Jones said.

evidence.supports: site just off Madison-Athens highway, about a mile NE of Apalachee
evidence.quote: The tower will be located just off the Madison-Athens highway about a mile northeast of Apalachee.
The holes for the tower will be dug starting next week on land donated by Marion Cochran, of Apalachee.

evidence.supports: three full-time towers plus two manned in critical periods
evidence.quote: The new tower will give Morgan and Walton three full-time fire towers plus two more which are manned in critical fire periods.

evidence.supports: Apalachee entry in Morgan County, elevation 681, GFC number

sources.title: Apalachee - Forest Lookouts (quoting The Madisonian, January 24, 1957)

notes_for_editor: Only the January 1957 announcement is sourced. No source confirms the move was completed, the tower's later history, or whether it still stands; the story says nothing about that beyond 'no source we found'. Unverified lead, deliberately left out of the story: a Facebook group comment (https://www.facebook.com/groups/596882218044256/permalink/1556921755373626/) says the Apalachee tower was bought, moved and is now on a private horse farm in Ocala, Florida. The page would not load in our reader and the claim could not be checked, so it is not cited; if a human can verify it, it is the most important fact missing. Record status 'unknown' and access 'unknown' were left unchanged. The 'three full-time towers' sentence describes the county network the move would create, not this tower's staffing, so it is not in facts.staffing. Record height_m 30.5 matches the article's 100 feet. Original site at Bostwick could merit its own record. The tower list gives its elevation (681) with no unit, so the story gives it without a conversion.
